tools.description: Compile context fragments into a token-budgeted, provenance-audited prompt context — deterministic, no LLM call. Duplicates drop, repeated log lines collapse, code/URLs/numbers/negative constraints survive verbatim, over-budget content becomes retrievable ctx://source/ handles; `memory_scope` pulls stored memories in. Fragment `metadata` ≤64 KiB. A fragment may set `path` (absolute file, UTF-8 ≤1 MiB; requires VELESDB_MEMORY_INGEST_ROOTS) INSTEAD of `content` — `content`+`media` may combine (content = the image's caption). Returns the assembled content, one auditable decision per fragment (rule id, reason, risk), sources, handles, token-savings, and `warnings` (externalized fragments worth a second look — empty is NOT a clean bill of health; `decisions` is the exhaustive record, `risk` the cheap second signal). `policy.slim_response` drops sections/decisions (keep off when the audit trail matters); `policy.ids_as_strings` stringifies id fields for u64-unsafe clients.

items.description: One unit of caller-supplied context to compile.

content.description:
The fragment text. `#[serde(default)]`: a `path` fragment carries no
`content` on the wire — the adapter resolves `path` into `content`
before the compiler core sees the request.

id.description:
Caller-side identifier; when absent, the compiler derives a stable
content-addressed id (`super::fragment_id`). Accepts a JSON number
or decimal string (`wire::deserialize_optional_id`) — a `fragment_id`
received as a string can be resubmitted unchanged.

kind.description:
Free-form kind hint (`"code"`, `"log"`, `"prose"`, …) — classification
works without it, but honors it when present.

media.description:
Inline media payload (US-009, PR1). `None` (the default) keeps every
pre-0.9.0 request wire-compatible. When set, the fragment packs as one
atomic piece — see `MediaRef`.

bytes_b64.description:
Raw media bytes, base64 (standard alphabet, padded). Capped at
`crate::limits::MAX_MEDIA_BYTES` and validated at compile time —
oversized or malformed is rejected before any other work.

mime.description:
Declared MIME type (e.g. `"image/png"`, `"image/jpeg"`). Only PNG/JPEG
headers are sniffed for dimensions; anything else falls back to a
deterministic over-count — never rejected for the mime alone.

metadata.description:
Caller metadata. Recognized keys: `"verbatim": true` forces
`ContextAction::Preserve`; `"cache": true` forces
`ContextAction::Cache`.

path.description:
Read this file's content from disk instead of inline `content` (V2b-1
path ingestion). `path` is EXCLUSIVE — it resolves into `content`
before the compiler core runs, so `path` + `content`/`media` is
rejected; `content` + `media` is the intended image+caption shape. A
fragment with none of the three is rejected too. Requires
`VELESDB_MEMORY_INGEST_ROOTS` set (a path-list allowlist of
directories), else every `path` fragment fails with "ingestion
disabled". Must be absolute and resolve (after symlinks) to a UTF-8
file under a configured root, ≤
`crate::limits::MAX_INGEST_FILE_BYTES`. The **pure compiler core
never reads this field** — resolution is an adapter-side I/O
pre-pass; an unresolved `path` reaching it is rejected with
`crate::error::MemoryError::IngestDisabled`.

memory_scope.description: Which memories may be pulled in (US-002; ignored by the memoryless core).

graph_boost.description:
Fusion weight added to graph-reached memories (default 0.15). Raise
it (e.g. `0.5`–`0.8`) when pulling curated fact chains built with
`relate`: evidence sharing **no vocabulary** with the query can then
out-rank lexical near-misses.

hops.description:
Graph-walk depth of the fused recall (default 2). Deeper hops reach
longer cause/fix chains from the vector seed.

project.description: Restrict recalled memories to this project facet.

policy.description: Per-request policy override; `None` uses the compiler's policy.

chunk.description:
How oversized fragments split before packing. Only
`ChunkPolicy::max_chunk_bytes` and `ChunkPolicy::boundary` apply
here — the compiler forces `overlap_bytes` to `0` (concatenated
pieces; an overlap prefix would duplicate verbatim content).

boundary.description:
Preferred cut points.
- "paragraph": Cut at blank lines (`\n\n`), falling back to hard splits inside an
oversized paragraph.
- "sentence": Cut after sentence enders (`.`, `!`, `?` followed by whitespace).
- "fixed": Cut at the byte ceiling only (char-aligned).

max_chunk_bytes.description: Soft byte ceiling per chunk (fences may exceed it, see module doc).

overlap_bytes.description:
Bytes of the previous chunk to repeat at the start of the next one
(char-aligned). `0` keeps chunks disjoint.

disabled_rules.description:
Rule ids to disable (e.g. `"abstract.log_dedup"`). Disabled rules are
skipped during classification; their fragments fall through to the
next matching rule.

event_ttl_seconds.description: TTL applied to compilation events (`None` keeps them).

ids_as_strings.description:
Wire-compat opt-in for the MCP context tools: when `true`, every
`super::wire::ID_KEYS` response field (`fragment_id`,
`content_hash`, `memory_id`, `fragment_ids`) is rewritten to decimal
strings — the same walk the Node/WASM bindings apply
(`super::wire::stringify_id_fields`). A raw MCP client parses ids
as JS `number`s, which lose precision above 2^53; strings round-trip
exactly. Default `false`: byte-identical numeric response unless
opted in.

importance.description:
Memory bridge only: usage-driven importance blend over the pulled
memories (RL confidence + batch-relative recency). The struct-level
`#[serde(default)]` keeps 0.8.0 requests wire-compatible.

confidence.description:
Weight of the learned RL confidence (fed by `feedback`). A memory
with no feedback history counts as neutral `0.5`, contributing `0`.
Default `0.2`.

recency.description:
Weight of the batch-relative recency term. Inert unless
`Self::recency_field` is also set. Default `0.1`.

recency_field.description:
Caller metadata key holding each memory's **numeric** timestamp-like
value; `None` disables the recency term. Must be monotone and
homogeneous across the batch (e.g. `YYYYMMDD` integers or an epoch)
— documented, not verified. Min-max normalised over memories carrying
the key; one without it contributes `0`, and a degenerate batch
(`max == min`) contributes `0` for all.

near_dup_dedup.description:
Collapse near-duplicates (case/whitespace variants) in addition to
exact duplicates. Default `true`.

normalize_log_timestamps.description:
Opt-in: before `abstract.log_dedup` groups a `kind = "log"`
fragment's repeated lines, mask each line's volatile prefix
(ISO/syslog timestamps, hex/pid counters) with **fixed** patterns —
never caller-supplied regex — so lines identical modulo timestamp
collapse into one annotated line (the first occurrence's exact bytes;
only the grouping key changes). Default `false`: opt-in because it
changes what "duplicate" means. See the README's "Normalizing
timestamped logs".

pricing.description:
Caller-supplied pricing table so insights report the estimated cost
avoided for `target_model` — the wire channel for cost accounting
(bindings cannot reach the Rust-only `with_pricing` builder). Takes
precedence over a builder-injected table. `None` reports tokens only.

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency code of every rate in the table (e.g. `"EUR"`).

additionalProperties.description:
Pricing of one model, in integer micro-units per **million** input tokens
(e.g. a `3 USD / 1M tokens` rate is `3_000_000`).

input_micros_per_million_tokens.description: Micro-units of the table's currency per million input tokens.

models.description:
Rates keyed by model name (a `BTreeMap` so iteration — and therefore
every serialized output — is deterministically ordered).

version.description:
Caller-side version tag of this table (recorded in insights so a cost
figure is always traceable to the prices that produced it).

record_events.description:
Memory bridge only: record a compilation event (metadata and hashes,
**never fragment content**) so savings stay aggregatable. Default
`true`; set `false` to opt out entirely.

response_reserve_tokens.description:
Tokens kept aside for the model's answer; the compiler packs into
`token_budget − response_reserve_tokens`. Default `0`: the caller
knows their generation length, the compiler does not guess it.

slim_response.description:
When `true`, `sections` and `decisions` are emptied out of the
response (`content`, `insights`, `risk`, `warnings`, `sources`,
`retrieval_handles` unaffected). The full audit trail stays
recoverable by re-compiling without it — compilation is
deterministic. Default `false`.

source_ttl_seconds.description: TTL applied to stored sources (`None` keeps them until forgotten).

store_sources.description:
Memory bridge only: store each distinct fragment's original (as an
internal system fact, invisible to normal recall) so its
`ctx://source/<hash>` handle round-trips. Default `true`.

project.description: Project facet, recorded in provenance and used by the memory bridge.

query.description: What the agent is working on — drives relevance scoring.

target_model.description:
Target model name — selects the row of the pricing table
(`CompilePolicy::pricing` on the wire, or the Rust
`super::ContextCompiler::with_pricing` builder) for cost insights.
Without a table, insights report tokens only.

Force one-line-one-turn JSONL parsing — a line that does not parse as
a `{role, content}` object is a hard error, never a silent fallback.

segments.description:
Every segment, in transcript order, with byte ranges that partition
the transcript exactly — no gaps, no overlaps. Edge case: a `jsonl`
line whose decoded content exceeds 1 MiB is re-split, and each child
gets a proportional share of the raw line span, not a byte-exact one.

items.description:
One entry of `SegmentationReport::segments` — the audit trail of how
`compile_transcript` cut the transcript up, independent of what
`compile_context` then did with the resulting fragments.

byte_end.description:
End byte offset (exclusive) in the original transcript. Same caveat
as `byte_start`.

byte_start.description:
Start byte offset (inclusive) in the original transcript. For `jsonl`
this is a slice of the raw JSON line's span, not of decoded
`content` — when one line's decoded content is re-split, each child's
range is a proportional, non-overlapping share of the raw range, not
byte-exact. Ranges still never overlap.

fragment_id.description:
The id this segment's fragment carries into `context.decisions` —
content-addressed, same formula as every other `compile_context`
fragment with no caller-supplied `id`.

index.description:
Position of this segment in `segmentation.segments`, in transcript
order.

oneOf.description:
Ordinary text — `ContextFragment::kind` stays `None`, so the
existing classification rules (code fence, URL, negative constraint,
value density, …) decide its fate exactly as for `compile_context`.

A triple-backtick-fenced block, cut out atomically by
`chunk::fence_segments`. Tagged `kind = "code"` so
`classify::classify`'s `preserve.code_fence` rule matches
even for a fence whose content does not itself literally contain
`` ``` `` (defense in depth; it usually does).

A run of at least `MIN_LOG_RUN_LINES` log-like lines. Tagged
`kind = "log"` so `abstract.log_dedup` can consider it for
repeated-line collapsing exactly like a caller-declared `kind: "log"`
fragment in `compile_context`.

role.description:
The turn's role, when one was determined. `null` for a `plain`
transcript with no matching marker at all.

turn.description: Which turn (0-based) this segment belongs to.

tools.description: Aggregate the token (and cost) savings of past compile_context calls, optionally per project. Figures are local estimates recorded per compilation (metadata only, never content); `truncated` reports when the sweep hit the recall cap.

project.description: Restrict the aggregation to this project facet.

tools.name: context_savings

cost_saved_micros_by_currency.description:
Estimated cost avoided, in micro-units, keyed by currency (events
priced under different pricing tables never silently mix).

tokens_in.description: Sum of estimated input tokens across events.

tokens_out.description: Sum of estimated output tokens across events.

tokens_saved.description: Sum of estimated tokens saved across events.

truncated.description:
`true` when the aggregation hit the recall cap
(`crate::limits::MAX_RECALL_LIMIT`) — older events beyond the cap
were not folded in.

tools.description: Look up a NAMED ENTITY (person, place, organisation): its attributes, outgoing (`relations`) and incoming (`relations_in`) typed edges — both directions, since a question is only answerable from one side. Use for questions ABOUT a thing ("how old is Theo", "who is Theo's father"), where `recall` only returns sentences mentioning the name. Entities/edges are auto-built by `remember_extracted` from text relationships (`X is the father of Y`) and properties (`Y is 15`), JSON types preserved. Name match is case-insensitive; the id is content-addressed, stable across sessions. `found: false` when never mentioned; `name` echoes canonicalized. Autograph edges land asynchronously. Relay ids as strings (`id_str`).

name.description: Entity name to look up. Matched case-insensitively.

tools.name: entity

attributes.description: Attributes learned about this entity, reserved keys stripped.

found.description: Whether an entity is known under that name at all.

id.description: Stable, content-addressed id of the entity (`0` when not found).

name.description:
Canonical (trimmed, lowercased) entity name. Always filled in — on a
MISS it echoes the *queried* name canonicalized, so a caller can pair
each response with its question (#1654).

items.description:
Wire shape of one typed edge leaving an entity, with the `target_id_str`
twin (issue #1468).

predicate.description: The edge label the passage stated (e.g. `"pere de"`, `"soeur de"`).

target.description: Stored content of the far end — for an entity, `Entity: <name>`.

target_id.description: Stable id of the entity (or fact) on the far end.

relations_in.description:
Typed edges pointing AT this entity, each naming its SOURCE — the
incoming side (e.g. `camille --soeur de--> theo` shows here on
Theo's profile). Nothing is inferred; this reports only what is
stored.

items.description:
Wire shape of one typed edge leaving an entity, with the `target_id_str`
twin (issue #1468).

predicate.description: The edge label the passage stated (e.g. `"pere de"`, `"soeur de"`).

target.description: Stored content of the far end — for an entity, `Entity: <name>`.

target_id.description: Stable id of the entity (or fact) on the far end.

relations_in_truncated.description:
Whether `relations_in` is a PARTIAL view — the incoming mirror of
`relations_truncated`.

relations_truncated.description:
Whether `relations` is a PARTIAL view — true when a response budget
cut the outgoing side; a list at exactly the cap is otherwise
indistinguishable (#1820).

tools.description: Explain why one fragment of a compile_context request was preserved, abstracted, externalized, dropped, or cached: the request is re-compiled deterministically (recording off) and the fragment's decision (rule id, reason, relevance, risk, handle) returned — no server state needed. Caveats: `memory_scope` recalls from CURRENT memory and a `path` fragment is re-read from CURRENT disk content — not necessarily what the original call saw. Prefer `fragment_index` (0-based) over `fragment_id` when fragments are byte-identical — a shared id resolves to the dedup survivor's decision. `policy.ids_as_strings` applies as in compile_context.

fragment_id.description:
The fragment whose decision to return, matched on
`ContextDecision::fragment_id` UNLESS `fragment_index` is also given.
Accepts a JSON number OR decimal string, so a `fragment_id` received
under `ids_as_strings` relays back unchanged.

fragment_index.description:
Optional 0-based position of the fragment in `request.fragments`;
when given, TAKES PRIORITY over `fragment_id`:
`decisions[fragment_index]` is unambiguous even when byte-identical
fragments share one content-addressed `fragment_id` (a plain lookup
returns the FIRST, the dedup survivor — never a dropped twin's).
Absent: lookup by `fragment_id` alone.

request.description:
The compile request to explain (compilation is deterministic, so
re-submitting the request reproduces the exact decisions).

items.description: One unit of caller-supplied context to compile.

content.description:
The fragment text. `#[serde(default)]`: a `path` fragment carries no
`content` on the wire — the adapter resolves `path` into `content`
before the compiler core sees the request.

id.description:
Caller-side identifier; when absent, the compiler derives a stable
content-addressed id (`super::fragment_id`). Accepts a JSON number
or decimal string (`wire::deserialize_optional_id`) — a `fragment_id`
received as a string can be resubmitted unchanged.

kind.description:
Free-form kind hint (`"code"`, `"log"`, `"prose"`, …) — classification
works without it, but honors it when present.

media.description:
Inline media payload (US-009, PR1). `None` (the default) keeps every
pre-0.9.0 request wire-compatible. When set, the fragment packs as one
atomic piece — see `MediaRef`.

bytes_b64.description:
Raw media bytes, base64 (standard alphabet, padded). Capped at
`crate::limits::MAX_MEDIA_BYTES` and validated at compile time —
oversized or malformed is rejected before any other work.

mime.description:
Declared MIME type (e.g. `"image/png"`, `"image/jpeg"`). Only PNG/JPEG
headers are sniffed for dimensions; anything else falls back to a
deterministic over-count — never rejected for the mime alone.

metadata.description:
Caller metadata. Recognized keys: `"verbatim": true` forces
`ContextAction::Preserve`; `"cache": true` forces
`ContextAction::Cache`.

path.description:
Read this file's content from disk instead of inline `content` (V2b-1
path ingestion). `path` is EXCLUSIVE — it resolves into `content`
before the compiler core runs, so `path` + `content`/`media` is
rejected; `content` + `media` is the intended image+caption shape. A
fragment with none of the three is rejected too. Requires
`VELESDB_MEMORY_INGEST_ROOTS` set (a path-list allowlist of
directories), else every `path` fragment fails with "ingestion
disabled". Must be absolute and resolve (after symlinks) to a UTF-8
file under a configured root, ≤
`crate::limits::MAX_INGEST_FILE_BYTES`. The **pure compiler core
never reads this field** — resolution is an adapter-side I/O
pre-pass; an unresolved `path` reaching it is rejected with
`crate::error::MemoryError::IngestDisabled`.

memory_scope.description: Which memories may be pulled in (US-002; ignored by the memoryless core).

graph_boost.description:
Fusion weight added to graph-reached memories (default 0.15). Raise
it (e.g. `0.5`–`0.8`) when pulling curated fact chains built with
`relate`: evidence sharing **no vocabulary** with the query can then
out-rank lexical near-misses.

hops.description:
Graph-walk depth of the fused recall (default 2). Deeper hops reach
longer cause/fix chains from the vector seed.

project.description: Restrict recalled memories to this project facet.

policy.description: Per-request policy override; `None` uses the compiler's policy.

chunk.description:
How oversized fragments split before packing. Only
`ChunkPolicy::max_chunk_bytes` and `ChunkPolicy::boundary` apply
here — the compiler forces `overlap_bytes` to `0` (concatenated
pieces; an overlap prefix would duplicate verbatim content).

boundary.description:
Preferred cut points.
- "paragraph": Cut at blank lines (`\n\n`), falling back to hard splits inside an
oversized paragraph.
- "sentence": Cut after sentence enders (`.`, `!`, `?` followed by whitespace).
- "fixed": Cut at the byte ceiling only (char-aligned).

max_chunk_bytes.description: Soft byte ceiling per chunk (fences may exceed it, see module doc).

overlap_bytes.description:
Bytes of the previous chunk to repeat at the start of the next one
(char-aligned). `0` keeps chunks disjoint.

disabled_rules.description:
Rule ids to disable (e.g. `"abstract.log_dedup"`). Disabled rules are
skipped during classification; their fragments fall through to the
next matching rule.

event_ttl_seconds.description: TTL applied to compilation events (`None` keeps them).

ids_as_strings.description:
Wire-compat opt-in for the MCP context tools: when `true`, every
`super::wire::ID_KEYS` response field (`fragment_id`,
`content_hash`, `memory_id`, `fragment_ids`) is rewritten to decimal
strings — the same walk the Node/WASM bindings apply
(`super::wire::stringify_id_fields`). A raw MCP client parses ids
as JS `number`s, which lose precision above 2^53; strings round-trip
exactly. Default `false`: byte-identical numeric response unless
opted in.

importance.description:
Memory bridge only: usage-driven importance blend over the pulled
memories (RL confidence + batch-relative recency). The struct-level
`#[serde(default)]` keeps 0.8.0 requests wire-compatible.

confidence.description:
Weight of the learned RL confidence (fed by `feedback`). A memory
with no feedback history counts as neutral `0.5`, contributing `0`.
Default `0.2`.

recency.description:
Weight of the batch-relative recency term. Inert unless
`Self::recency_field` is also set. Default `0.1`.

recency_field.description:
Caller metadata key holding each memory's **numeric** timestamp-like
value; `None` disables the recency term. Must be monotone and
homogeneous across the batch (e.g. `YYYYMMDD` integers or an epoch)
— documented, not verified. Min-max normalised over memories carrying
the key; one without it contributes `0`, and a degenerate batch
(`max == min`) contributes `0` for all.

near_dup_dedup.description:
Collapse near-duplicates (case/whitespace variants) in addition to
exact duplicates. Default `true`.

normalize_log_timestamps.description:
Opt-in: before `abstract.log_dedup` groups a `kind = "log"`
fragment's repeated lines, mask each line's volatile prefix
(ISO/syslog timestamps, hex/pid counters) with **fixed** patterns —
never caller-supplied regex — so lines identical modulo timestamp
collapse into one annotated line (the first occurrence's exact bytes;
only the grouping key changes). Default `false`: opt-in because it
changes what "duplicate" means. See the README's "Normalizing
timestamped logs".

pricing.description:
Caller-supplied pricing table so insights report the estimated cost
avoided for `target_model` — the wire channel for cost accounting
(bindings cannot reach the Rust-only `with_pricing` builder). Takes
precedence over a builder-injected table. `None` reports tokens only.

currency.description: ISO-4217 currency code of every rate in the table (e.g. `"EUR"`).

additionalProperties.description:
Pricing of one model, in integer micro-units per **million** input tokens
(e.g. a `3 USD / 1M tokens` rate is `3_000_000`).

input_micros_per_million_tokens.description: Micro-units of the table's currency per million input tokens.

models.description:
Rates keyed by model name (a `BTreeMap` so iteration — and therefore
every serialized output — is deterministically ordered).

version.description:
Caller-side version tag of this table (recorded in insights so a cost
figure is always traceable to the prices that produced it).

record_events.description:
Memory bridge only: record a compilation event (metadata and hashes,
**never fragment content**) so savings stay aggregatable. Default
`true`; set `false` to opt out entirely.

response_reserve_tokens.description:
Tokens kept aside for the model's answer; the compiler packs into
`token_budget − response_reserve_tokens`. Default `0`: the caller
knows their generation length, the compiler does not guess it.

slim_response.description:
When `true`, `sections` and `decisions` are emptied out of the
response (`content`, `insights`, `risk`, `warnings`, `sources`,
`retrieval_handles` unaffected). The full audit trail stays
recoverable by re-compiling without it — compilation is
deterministic. Default `false`.

source_ttl_seconds.description: TTL applied to stored sources (`None` keeps them until forgotten).

store_sources.description:
Memory bridge only: store each distinct fragment's original (as an
internal system fact, invisible to normal recall) so its
`ctx://source/<hash>` handle round-trips. Default `true`.

project.description: Project facet, recorded in provenance and used by the memory bridge.

query.description: What the agent is working on — drives relevance scoring.

target_model.description:
Target model name — selects the row of the pricing table
(`CompilePolicy::pricing` on the wire, or the Rust
`super::ContextCompiler::with_pricing` builder) for cost insights.
Without a table, insights report tokens only.

token_budget.description: Hard token ceiling for the assembled content.

tools.name: explain_compilation

oneOf.description: Emitted verbatim — critical content (code, constraints, exact values).

Emitted as a deterministic structured reduction (never a generative
summary) — e.g. repeated log lines collapsed with a count.
Not emitted, but recoverable through its `ctx://source/<id>` handle.
Not emitted and not externalized — redundant content (duplicates).

Emitted verbatim at the front of the output, forming a stable prefix
that maximizes provider prompt-cache hits across compilations.

content_hash.description:
Content hash of the *original* fragment text (FNV-1a 64,
`super::fragment_id`) — proves which exact bytes the decision
covered even when the caller supplied its own id.

fragment_id.description: The fragment this decision is about (caller id, or content-derived).

handle.description: Recoverable address of the original content, when not fully emitted.

memory_id.description: The memory backing this fragment, when it came from recall (US-002).

relevance.description: Lexical relevance of the fragment to the request query, in `[0, 1]`.

risk.description: Fidelity risk this single decision contributes.

oneOf.description: Nothing was lost: everything fit, only exact duplicates were dropped.

Recoverable reductions happened: abstractions, or non-critical
fragments externalized behind retrieval handles.

Critical content (a preserve-classified fragment) could not be packed
— the caller should consider retrieving it or raising the budget.

rule_id.description: The stable id of the rule that decided (e.g. `"preserve.code_fence"`).

tools.description: Read one durable extraction job by the `request_id` returned from `remember_extracted`. Returns that `request_id`, its persisted `state` (`accepted`, `running`, `committed`, or `failed`), committed fact `ids` and their u64-safe decimal `ids_str` twins, `skipped_over_cap` after commit, and `error` after failure. While accepted/running, `ids` and `ids_str` are empty and both optional terminal fields are null.
tools.name: extraction_status

error.description: Terminal failure detail, present only in the `failed` state.

ids.description: Stored fact ids after commit; empty while pending or failed.

ids_str.description: Decimal-string twins of `ids` for float-lossy JSON clients.

skipped_over_cap.description:
Extracted facts dropped for exceeding the embeddable cap, present only
after commit.

tools.description: Reinforce a recalled memory with an outcome: `success=true` if the fact was useful, `false` if it was noise. This durably updates the fact's learned confidence, which `recall` uses to re-rank future results — over repeated feedback, useful facts drift up and noise drifts down, so the memory improves with use without retraining the model. Concurrent feedback on one fact is applied atomically, each call counted once. Returns the fact's new confidence in [0,1].

id.description:
Id of the recalled memory to reinforce (as returned by
`recall`/`remember`). Accepts a JSON number or a decimal string —
relay `id_str` to avoid float-precision loss above 2^53 (issue
#1468).

success.description:
`true` if the memory was useful (reinforce it), `false` if it was noise
(weaken it).

tools.name: feedback

confidence.description: The memory's new learned confidence in `[0.0, 1.0]` after this feedback.

tools.description: Permanently delete a memory by `id`, removing the fact and its graph links — durable, irreversible. For time-based expiry use `remember`'s TTL instead. Returns the id plus `found`: true = deleted, false = nothing stored under that id (no-op, not an error).

id.description:
Id of the memory to permanently delete (as returned by `remember` or
`recall`). Accepts a JSON number or a decimal string — relay `id_str`
to avoid float-precision loss above 2^53 (issue #1468).

tools.name: forget

found.description:
Whether a memory actually existed under `id` and was deleted.
`false` means nothing was stored there — a stale id or a typo, not a
second successful deletion — so a caller can tell the two apart.

id.description: Id that was requested for deletion.

tools.description: AUDIT the store: page through every stored fact — what `recall` cannot answer (it only ranks by resemblance). Use for 'what do you know about me/this project?', cleanup before sharing, or backup. Returns `memories` (ids ascending; each entry carries `id`, `id_str`, `content`, `metadata`) and `next_cursor`: pass it as `cursor` for the next page, null = done. `filter` keeps facts matching every key; a sparse page is not the end — KEEP following `next_cursor`. `include_internal` also lists internal scaffolding verbatim. Ids exceed 2^53 — relay as strings.

cursor.description:
Resume the walk strictly after this id — the `next_cursor` of the
previous page. Omit to start from the beginning. Accepts a JSON
number or a decimal string (issue #1468).

filter.description:
Keep only facts whose metadata equals every given key, e.g.
`{"project": "acme"}`. A filtered page may come back sparse — keep
following `next_cursor`; the walk stays exhaustive.

include_internal.description:
Also list internal graph scaffolding (entity hubs) and reserved
`_veles_*` keys, verbatim. Default `false`: the audit shows the
user's facts as `recall` would show them.

tools.name: list_memories

memories.description: This page of the walk, ids ascending.

items.description: One entry of `ListMemoriesResult`.

metadata.description:
Metadata under the same visibility policy as `recall` (business keys
plus the auto-stamped `_veles_date`), or the raw payload when
`include_internal` was set. `null` when nothing survives.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` to get the next page; `null` means the walk is
complete.

Project facet to list saved working-context sessions for (same
convention as `save_working_context`'s `project`).

Every session saved under this project, most-recently-saved first.

saved_at.description:

`save_working_context`, not just the first (a resave never
duplicates). `0` on wasm (no clock); the most-recent-first order is

session is the case the caller can least detect. Empty only when the

embedder.description: Which embedder is running and whether recall is semantic.

The vector width the embedder produces. Reported with the model so a
mismatch diagnosis never needs a second call.

offline embedder, otherwise as configured (`bge-m3`, `all-minilm`).

(a binding constructing `McpServer` directly).

Whether recall is SEMANTIC. `false` means the `hash` embedder:
surface-form matching, not meaning — the most common "why is recall
bad?" answer. `null` when no identity was declared.

autograph_active.description:
Whether the background autograph worker is consuming the queue
(#1846): `remember`'s graph enrichment runs behind the response.

autograph_dropped.description:
Enrichments refused by a FULL queue since startup — the facts were
stored, only their wiring was skipped (#1846's counted-drop rule).

autograph_failed.description:
Enrichments that RAN and failed part-way since startup — the fact is
stored, its graph structure partial; re-remembering completes it.
Distinct from `autograph_dropped` (never ran).

configured.description:

a numeric `20230101` never matches `"20230101"` stored as a string —

`MemoryService::recall_where`.

value.description:
Value to compare against.

The comparison is TYPE-STRICT with no coercion, so the JSON type sent
here is part of the query: `20260601` (number) never matches a fact
stored as `"20260601"` (string) — same value, no match, and **no
error**. A wrong type here is therefore the one mistake this API
cannot report; it just returns nothing.

Which is why the advertised type is spelled out rather than left as
the empty schema `serde_json::Value` would produce. `{}` says "send
anything", on the single field where sending the wrong thing fails
silently.

tools.description: Store a fact in durable local memory; optional `links` (graph edges) and `metadata` tags (ColumnStore, ≤64 KiB serialized) for later filtering. Optional `anchors` (repo-relative paths, ≤8) with `anchor_root` (an absolute checkout inside the server's ingest roots, validated even without `anchors`) tie the fact to those files in that checkout: the server records each file's SHA-256 so a later `recall` with the same checkout can flag the fact stale when one changes; re-remember with `anchors` to re-anchor.
